transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-10-06
Start: 10:30 AM PT
Duration: ~90 minutes
Attendees: Maya (AE), Ravi (SE), Jonas (Enablement), Elena, Sam, Diego (Regional SEs/AEs)

Optional auto sections: Summary present, Topics present, Action items present

[00:00:00] Maya: "All right, thanks everyone for hopping on. Quick check, audio ok?"
[00:00:06] Elena: "Yeah good, can hear you."
[00:00:09] Ravi: "loud and clear."
[00:00:12] Maya: "Cool. Today is a battlecard wargame plus live demo lab — want to tighten the two-pager and practice the 6-minute demo script we landed on. We'll do three roleplay rounds, each with a different competitive angle. Keep it high tempo."
[00:00:28] Sam: "Sounds good — also want to make sure we cover dedicated vs hosted pitch for mid-market. I'm getting mid-market asking for predictable throughput but not always willing to pay for reserved capacity."
[00:00:39] Jonas: "Noted, we'll keep a concise tradeoff line."

[00:00:45] --- Topic 1: Battlecard structure ---
[00:00:46] Maya: "Okay quick show of the draft: headline value (production economics + predictable SLOs), 3 bullets on differentiators, then rebuttals, proof points (benchmarks), and ask/CTA. Anybody think that's missing something?"
[00:00:58] Elena: "Can we add a one-line on "unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private" — that's the hook that closes a lot of platform buyers."
[00:01:06] Maya: "Yes, add that. Make it the first bullet after the headline."
[00:01:10] Ravi: "Also include a simple visual: a switch showing hosted -> dedicated -> private with icons and a single sentence describing when to pick each. Visuals help AEs."
[00:01:18] Sam: "And a short rebuttal against "we can self-host cheaper" — something like "self-hosting often has hidden ops cost and variance in latency; Redwood's runtime and routing reduce per-token costs at scale.""
[00:01:30] Diego: "throw in KV cache + batching as the secret sauce line, customers love that."

[00:01:35] --- Topic 2: Competitive plays ---
[00:01:36] Maya: "We'll run three plays. Play A: Anthropic price/perf angle. Play B: Bedrock/Cloud vendor consolidation. Play C: OpenAI feature parity + ecosystem."
[00:01:46] Elena: "For Anthropic, emphasize throughput and deployment flexibility. They position on safety and model quality, so counter with: "If you need predictable throughput or private deployments, Redwood gives the same model mix with operational SLAs.""
[00:02:01] Ravi: "Important to not claim model parity on safety — say: "We integrate curated models and Redwood-verified profiles; for safety-sensitive use cases we recommend private deployment + audit logs.""
[00:02:12] Maya: "Good, that wording."
[00:02:15] Sam: "Against Bedrock, the angle is vendor lock and pricing complexity. We say: "Redwood offers consistent API and routing across clouds and private infra — reduces vendor lock and brings cost transparency.""
[00:02:28] Jonas: "Call out that Bedrock often has delta in latency depending on region, and our smart routing + fallback reduces user-visible errors."

[00:02:38] --- Demo prep / canonical walkthrough ---
[00:02:40] Ravi: "Here's the 6-minute demo flow I'm going to run: 0:00–0:30 quick product statement and value prop; 0:30–1:30 live API call (streaming) to show low latency; 1:30–3:00 show model catalog and version pinning w/ rollout example; 3:00–4:00 show Dedicated config (pool sizing + autoscale); 4:00–5:00 show observability dashboards (token cost + latency breakdown); 5:00–6:00 handle a simulated failure and show automatic fallback to cheaper model variant."
[00:03:12] Maya: "Tight — keep the streaming example short and pick a prompt that surfaces hallucination mitigation and structured output."
[00:03:19] Elena: "What's the exact prompt? If it's too generic we lose the audience."
[00:03:22] Ravi: "I'll use a finance compliance example: "Given this customer support ticket, extract PII fields and synthesize a short redaction summary." That shows structured output and tool-calling style behavior."
[00:03:31] Sam: "Nice. Also have a one-line to compare token cost before/after batching."

[00:03:38] --- Roleplay Round 1: Anthropic objection ---
[00:03:40] Maya (AE -> Sam playing prospect): "We're evaluating Anthropic because of their model quality — why would we pick Redwood?"
[00:03:48] Sam (as prospect): "We care about both quality and predictable latency."
[00:03:52] Maya: "Totally — Redwood is model-agnostic, we surface curated variants and pick kernels at runtime so you get consistent latency at scale. We also have Dedicated pools if you need strict SLOs and predictable throughput."
[00:04:05] Sam: "But Anthropic says their models are better for safety — how do you respond?"
[00:04:08] Maya: "We don't claim model-level safety leadership; instead we give you the controls: private deployment, audit logs, and the ability to pin tested model versions so your compliance team can validate outputs before rollouts."
[00:04:20] Elena: (whispers) might want to add a line about evals and regression alerts.

[00:04:26] --- Roleplay Round 2: Bedrock consolidation objection ---
[00:04:28] Diego (playing prospect): "We already use Bedrock for internal projects — why add Redwood?"
[00:04:32] Jonas: "You can keep Bedrock as a model source; Redwood acts as the unified runtime that normalizes APIs, gives you consistent routing policies, and reduces per-token cost with batching and prefix caching. It removes the integration maintenance from your platform team."
[00:04:46] Diego: "What about data residency? Bedrock has regions — how do you manage?"
[00:04:50] Ravi: "We support private deployment and VPC connectors plus customer-managed KMS for keys; that lets you keep data in-region while using the Redwood control plane."

[00:04:57] --- Roleplay Round 3: Cost objection (we can self-host) ---
[00:04:59] Sam: "We could just run open models ourselves and save money."
[00:05:02] Maya: "Short answer: sometimes, but often the ops, variance in latency, and ongoing optimization work outweigh the infra savings. Our Optimize toolkit recommends quantization and batching profiles tuned to your workload so you get near self-host cost with less ops overhead."
[00:05:16] Elena: "Add a data point: share a post-pilot number where batching reduced token costs by 30% for a conversational workload."
[00:05:22] Maya: "Agree — keep it generic: 'customer X saw ~30% per-token reduction after applying profile recommendations.' Don't use actual customer name unless it's approved."

[00:05:30] --- Live demo run (Ravi) ---
[00:05:32] [00:05:32] Ravi: Starting the demo screen share now — ping if you don't see it.
[00:05:37] Elena: We see it. Buffering a bit but watching.
[00:05:41] Ravi: Hitting the streaming endpoint: sending a prompt to detect PII and synthesize a redaction summary... [00:05:55] Response streaming in, latency ~120ms for first tokens — note that number, it's what we want to show.
[00:06:05] Jonas: Could we also show token breakdown? Maybe a quick shot of the token accounting.
[00:06:09] Ravi: Sure — switching to the dashboard. You can see token counts per route and cost estimates per 1M tokens — red/green markers for constrained routes.
[00:06:20] Diego: Nice, the fallback example now?
[00:06:23] Ravi: Simulating a heavy load in region A, router fails over to variant model B — demo shows 200ms bump but no request errors.
[00:06:33] Sam: Good example of graceful degradation.

[00:06:36] --- Coaching notes in the moment ---
[00:06:37] Maya: Two coaching tips: 1) When asked about pricing, don't recite per-token numbers unless asked — frame as per-user per-month or per-conversation cost plus optimization levers. 2) Always probe for SLOs: "What's your target p95 latency?" That opens the route to Dedicated conversation.
[00:06:56] Elena: Also, when security is front-of-mind, lead with audit logs + KMS + SLA rather than cost.

[00:07:05] --- Objection scripts to memorize ---
[00:07:06] Maya: Short scripts: "Vendor lock" -> "Our routing and model catalog reduce lock by normalizing APIs and providing fallbacks"; "We self-host" -> "Our Optimize kit reduces ops and variance while giving you the option to run private infra"; "Better model" -> "We support curated models and evals to match your quality bar, plus rollouts".
[00:07:26] Sam: Maybe add one-liners for procurement questions — procurement often asks about SLAs, exit, and data deletion.
[00:07:33] Jonas: I'll add a procurement FAQ slide and a short script for 'what's in the contract'.

[00:07:40] --- Quick whiteboarding: demo script timings ---
[00:07:41] Ravi: Note — the streaming example must be sub-60 seconds in the demo to keep attention. Keep the failure simulation not too technical, high-level.
[00:07:51] Maya: We should standardize the demo prompt and keep a small set of two prompts: compliance PII extraction and e-commerce summarization. That covers both structured output and generation use cases.

[00:07:59] --- Audience-specific tweaks ---
[00:08:00] Elena: For EMEA, highlight data residency and regulatory posture earlier in the talk. For APAC, have a section on on-prem options.
[00:08:08] Diego: APAC buyers ask about burst capacity and GPU availability — be ready with capacity SLAs and burst policies.

[00:08:15] --- Misc: competitive fact checks ---
[00:08:17] Sam: Quick callouts: Anthropic recently published a safety paper (we should not misrepresent it), Bedrock pricing sometimes hides data transfer egress, OpenAI has strong developer mindshare. Use these carefully.
[00:08:29] Maya: Add one-liners to the battlecard that are safe: cite public docs rather than internal intel.

[00:08:36] --- Wrap and recap ---
[00:08:37] Maya: OK recap: Maya circulate updated battlecard + cheat-sheet; Ravi record canonical demo; Jonas add procurement FAQ + pricing bullets; Elena collect region objections; schedule roleplays with EMEA/APAC. Any other items?
[00:08:53] Elena: Could you also add a very short rubric for the roleplay grading? 1–5 for handling objection, 1–5 for demo tempo.
[00:09:00] Jonas: I'll add the rubric to Confluence.

[00:09:05] Maya: Great — meeting over. Thanks all.

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and filler words were left as-is to preserve realism. Some technical terms spelled as plain text (KV cache, VPC, KMS).
